Sarah — thanks for the note and great to hear the demo resonated. High-level answers up front:
- Execution can be constrained by region depending on deployment mode. For hosted evals we typically run in the cloud region you choose (us-east-1 / eu-west-1 / etc.) and we can pin requests to that region for the duration of the trial.
- Runtime subprocessors: we use a small set for networking/KMS/logging. I attached a simple execution map that shows the common hops (prefix caching, model runtime, telemetry router).
- EU-only evaluation: yes — we can route inference to eu-west-1 and ensure no cross-border egress from that runtime while the trial is active.

I'll loop Rafael in for the subprocessor roster and the technical controls (KMS, auth, telemetry retention). Attaching a one-page execution map now.

Sarah — digging into the technicals:

1) Typical hosted evaluation path (eu-west-1 pin):
   - Client -> Frontend API (eu-west-1) -> Router -> Model runtime pods (eu-west-1)
   - KMS calls for key material may call customer's KMS in-region (if configured) or Redwood-managed KMS in the same region
   - Telemetry/metrics: short-lived metrics are aggregated in-region; application logs are written to a telemetry router which is configured to keep data in-region for EU pins (we can enforce no replication to other regions during the eval)

2) Subprocessors that may touch requests during runtime:
   - Cloud provider infra (VM/instance hosts) — regional (AWS eu-west-1)
   - CDN / load balancer — regional endpoints
   - Telemetry/metrics vendor (ingest) — configured to operate in-region for EU trials
   - Optional: managed feature-store or vector DB (only if customer enables persistence), otherwise model input/output is transient in memory/KV cache

3) Retention and deletion for eval:
   - Runtime traces and request logs: default 30 days, can be reduced to 7 days for trials upon request.
   - Model cache / KV: ephemeral, TTL typically 1 hour in our eval config.
   - Persistent artifacts (if enabled): snapshot retention is governed by contract and can be disabled for trials.

4) Transfer assurances: for an EU-only evaluation we will:
   - Pin runtime to eu-west-1; disable cross-region replication for telemetry; configure telemetry vendor to store EU-only; and record the configuration in a short MOP (method of procedure) that we share.

I've attached the subprocessor roster CSV (redacted entries for partners that are region-specific) and a small note on retention controls. Happy to jump on a call to walk the team through it.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Sarah — quick summary and commitments for the trial so you can share with auditors/procurement:

- No-eGress statement for EU trial: Redwood will not send evaluation inference traffic pinned to eu-west-1 to any US-hosted analytics or logging endpoints for the duration of the trial. Telemetry ingestion will be configured to retain data in eu-west-1 only and cross-region replication is disabled.
- 7-day retention: we will apply a 7-day retention for request logs and runtime traces for this trial, including error dumps. Ephemeral KV caches are TTL-limited (1 hour) and not persisted beyond the retention window.
- Attestation doc: attached is a short attestation (summary MOP + subprocessor list excerpt) we maintain for evaluation runs; it includes the configuration flags and the person-of-contact for the audit.

Next steps: Rafael and I can join a 30-minute call with your security team to walk the MOP and sign off. Ben will follow up with a procurement checklist and a DocuSign link if BlueHaven wants us to sign a temporary addendum for EU-only eval routing.
